classification.difficultyReason: Allocate the remaining probability in a 1:1:2 ratio and turn the fractions into a valid spinner construction.

inlines.text: Construct a spinner with 4 colours (red, green, blue, and yellow) that meets these conditions:
The probability of landing on blue is
There is an equal chance of landing on red and green.
Landing on yellow is twice as likely to occur as landing on red.

answer.short: Blue $\frac13$, red $\frac16$, green $\frac16$, yellow $\frac13$. Six equal sectors: two blue, one red, one green and two yellow; other orders are valid.
answer.worked:
Let $P(R)=P(G)=x$.
$$\begin{align*}P(B)+P(R)+P(G)+P(Y)&=1\\\frac13+x+x+2x&=1\\4x&=\frac23\\x&=\frac16\end{align*}$$
Therefore the spinner should be $\frac13$ blue, $\frac16$ red, $\frac16$ green and $\frac13$ yellow.
Divide the circle into six equal sectors. Label two Blue, one Red, one Green and two Yellow. Other sector orders are valid.

spec.mathematics: Each sector subtends 60 degrees. Blue occupies two sectors, red one, green one and yellow two. Thus P(B)=1/3, P(R)=P(G)=1/6 and P(Y)=1/3=2P(R). Sector order is an authored example and is unrestricted.
